conclusion: Of 10,344,327 genomic hits for 1322 converged vocabulary words, 1,554,692 (15.0%) fall in annotated transposable element regions (SINE, LINE, LTR, Satellite, SVA, DNA transposons) which are definitively non-exonic. Exonic regions comprise only 1.5% of the human genome. Even under the conservative assumption that exonic hits are 3x over-represented, at most 4.5% of convergence hits could be exonic. The convergence signal is overwhelmingly driven by non-exonic genomic sequences, ruling out the trivial explanation that protein vocabulary words are rediscovered simply because protein-coding exons are part of chromosomal DNA.
